messages:
maria (People Ops): Hey team — quick Q about an employee who changed payroll jurisdiction mid-year (US -> UK) and we had a payroll provider cutover in the same window. They were contributing to the 401(k) pre-move and did a voluntary stop when they moved. Also they elected to stop HSA contributions when they left US healthcare. Need clarity on how to handle: proration of deferrals, catch-up eligibility (they're 50+), and whether we can / should push a retro adjustment for missed employer match across the two payroll systems. Any compliance or vendor gotchas?
kevin (Payroll): Thanks — can you share the date ranges? Cutover date and move date? Our vendor cutover on 2025-09-15 (pay cycle ended 9/12) — did employee move before or after final US paycheck?
sarah (Engineering): fwiw moving teams, not relevant but curious — did they change FTE or salary band? that can affect match math if employer match is % of base.
maria (People Ops): Move effective 2025-09-01, last US paycheck 2025-09-12 (paid), first UK payroll 2025-09-26. They stopped 401(k) deductions on 9/01 and HSA on 9/01. They turned 50 on 2025-04-10 so catch-up applies for whole year theoretically.
kevin (Payroll): Ok timeline helps. Two things: 1) Our 401(k) vendor can accept retro adjustments, but only if we submit within the quarter cutoff (we missed Q3 cutoff if send now). 2) Because cutover happened, there is a reconciliation flow — we can push a manual employer match via the old vendor but it requires signed authorization + payroll remittance. Also need employee SSN and payroll ID.
kevin (Payroll): Sample request we need: ``emp_id: 43219, ssn_last4: 6789, period: 2025-01-01 to 2025-09-12, gross_deferrals: 14,200, catchup_deferrals: 3,000`` — without that automation we'll need spreadsheets.
alex (Finance): Two compliance notes: a) Catch-up contributions are treated as elective deferrals but plan rules determine if partial-year catch-up is allowed — usually based on plan year, not service months. b) When employee moves to UK and becomes non-US tax resident, ongoing 401(k) deferrals stop, but retro employer match for the period they were eligible is typically allowed if properly remitted. We should confirm with vendor and legal for cross-border tax withholding on that match.
sarah (Engineering): Does the HSA stop change anything for employer match calc? They stopped HSA but match is 401k based so probably not.
maria (People Ops): Correct, HSA separate. Main ask: can we (1) calculate pro-rated match for Jan–Aug period, (2) apply catch-up for full year or pro-rate it, (3) push manual match payment through vendor even though cutover happened. I can collect the numbers but want to know policy before asking employee to sign anything.
kevin (Payroll): (1) yes we can calculate pro-rated match for contributions actually made (Jan–Sep payrolls). (2) catch-up eligibility: plan allows catch-up for whole plan year if employee attains 50 during the year — so they can make catch-up on their US payroll up to the plan limit, but since they left early we can only remit actual catch-up amounts withheld. We can't invent extra catch-up unless employee elected it and it was withheld. (3) manual match through previous vendor — possible but traction depends on vendor's reconciliation window. I'll open a ticket with them today but will need authorization PDF from Maria + finance remittance.
hr-bot: Policy excerpt: "401(k) employer match is calculated on elective deferrals actually remitted during the plan year. Catch-up contributions are permitted in accordance with IRS rules and plan document. Manual remittances for missed employer match may be accepted per vendor cutover terms; contact payroll and benefits for reconciliation." <https://docs.redwood.com/benefits/401k-policy#manual-remit>
maria (People Ops): Thanks. I'll gather the emp_id + SSN last4 + payroll export for Jan–Sep and ping the employee for a signature authorization template. Alex — can finance create a remittance line for manual match if vendor confirms acceptance?
alex (Finance): Yes we can. Please put estimated amount in this thread or DM me the sheet. We'll need GL code 6230 and cost center.
maria (People Ops): Bringing in numbers now: rough deferral total 14,200, catch-up 3,000, expected company match (3% of eligible wages) math = $3,020 — marking as estimate until payroll confirms. I'll follow up once payroll vendor responds. :thumbsup:
kevin (Payroll): I'll update here after vendor reply. If they require quarter cutoff exception, I'll escalate to vendor ops.
maria (People Ops): Great — thanks all. I'll post the signed auth once I have it and loop legal if vendor flags cross-border tax withholding.
